newsitem.title: INDONESIA: S.E. Asian Cocoa - Prices easier, supply tight.
newsitem.headline: S.E. Asian Cocoa - Prices easier, supply tight.

text.p: Southeast Asian cocoa prices were lower on Wednesday following steady declines in New York, while supply remained tight in Indonesia, traders said.
They said there were indications supply in the Malaysian market was getting thin because of a poor mid-year harvest, especially in the main growing area of Tawau due to bad weather.
"The supply is flat, with prices edging down because of New York," one Indonesian trader said. "Some players are even willing to pay a premium because supply is tight."
The trader said the weakening of the Indonesian currency against the U.S. dollar would boost the commodity's export competitiveness but added that tight supply posed limitations.

"It will give a competitive edge to fresh deals, but the problem is supply is very tight," the trader said. "One company is sitting pretty because it has a large amount of stocks and is selling to the United States."
The Indonesian rupiah plunged to a historic low of 2,665 against the dollar on Monday following offshore speculative attacks, but had since regained some strength.
Traders said some buyers were paying relatively high prices for beans to fill contracts.
"One player has cancelled all contracts he had concluded when prices were lower and is buying beans from his suppliers at higher prices to make sure he gets the beans," one trader said.
"The market is getting crazy and there is talk that one speculator had disappeared after having failed to supply beans at contracted prices," he added.
The trader said arrivals at Ujung Pandang, capital of the key growing region of South Sulawesi, were slow and expectations that supply would improve in August were waning.
Traders said cocoa was quoted at 3,300-3,350 rupiah/kg in Ujung Pandang, compared with 3,435-3,475 rupiah/kg a week ago.
In Malaysia, traders expected prices to move slightly higher after sharp falls over the past week.
"The market had fallen quite a fair bit but it is stabilising at the moment. It should go slightly higher," one trader said.
Weakness in world cocoa prices and rains in Malaysia's main cocoa growing area of Tawau in the eastern state of Sabah contributed to the recent fall in local prices, traders said.
Tawau had a long spell of dry weather in June that raised concern about crop prospects. Traders said talk of a poor domestic crop could provide some underlying support.
An industry official said there were indications the market was again getting short on beans due to weak harvests recently. "At the moment, the crop does not look encouraging," he said.
Growers in Tawau have said the mid-year harvest between April and June was drastically affected by rain, which destroyed pod setting earlier in the year.

On Wednesday, the Malaysian Cocoa Board quoted the SMC 1A grade cocoa beans out of Tawau at an average of 3,500 ringgit a tonne, down 143 ringgit from a week ago. The Grade 1B, also out of Tawau, was quoted by the board at an average of 3,405 ringgit, down 188 from last week.
